(1) reappraisal of the intentions of the proposer in the DG affects the neural response to the received offer; (2) the neural correlates of this reappraisal effect are the inferior and middle prefrontal cortex, temporo-parital junction and insula; (3) the middle frontal gyrust activation correlates with the frequency of reappraisal strategies used in daily life; (4) the insula activation correlates with the perceived ability of reappraisal; (5)

the neural effects of ER on social emotions were the inferior and the middle frontal gyruses, temporo-paraital junction and insulas bilaterally, and that the striatum, posterior cingulate, and the insula were the regulated regions.

reappraisal can modulate neural responses in regions that have been previously associated with ER strategies and socially driven emotions, and that the implementation of ER strategies is associated with individual differences.

understanding how we can control the emotional responses we have to social interactions.
the role of ER strategies on socially driven emotions, and how these are regulated by neural mechanisms.
the neural correlates of reappraisal, an ER strategy that is often used in daily life and in psychotherapeutic contexts.

reappraisal of social intentions is a powerful strategy for regulating social emotions, but the way we regulate these emotions may also depend on the way the social situation is appraised.

The main takeaway from our work is that

reappraisal of the intentions of others is an important factor to consider when studying and treating socially driven emotions, and that the neural mechanisms involved may be modulated by both the ability to use ER strategies and by the way others treat us.
reappraisal of the intentions of others can strongly affect the neural response to socially-driven emotions.
